context.objective: Document how we carry out Accounts Payable, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: To begin with, we receive and review the invoice. That is done by: Preparer. What we do: confirm the attachment is an invoice and identify the client/entity; record receipt for processing so the email is not missed; if the request is urgent, identify the requested timing and who must approve the exception. The check on it: every received invoice is added to the processing list. Next, we save the invoice PDF to Box. That is done by: Preparer. What we do: save the PDF in the approved client/entity Box location; use the applicable naming convention; link or reference the stored PDF in the operational log where the template supports it. The check on it: use the stored PDF as the source for approval, the Entrilia entry, and the final record comparison.
What happens to the invoice after you’ve saved the PDF in Box?

After that, we log and duplicate-check the invoice. That is done by: Preparer. What we do: enter vendor, invoice number, date, amount, entity, and status in the Excel invoice log; search existing records for the same vendor + invoice number + amount; resolve any possible duplicate before recording the invoice in Entrilia or paying it. The check on it: do not record or pay an invoice until any possible duplicate is resolved. Then, we determine coding and allocation. That is done by: Preparer; manager reviews. What we do: determine the correct general-ledger account and accounting class, and how the amount should be split among legal entities; apply only a current, client-approved allocation matrix where one exists; for One Rock matrix items, obtain the stated invoice-level support for line items above $1,000 only after the process owner or appropriate process expert confirms that the threshold and matrix version are current; document the reason for the coding and the supporting records needed for review. The check on it: manager reviews judgment-based coding before final approval/payment.
Once the manager has reviewed the coding and allocation, what happens next?
This capture still has open sections. 15 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.
One more thing: after the invoice is approved, the AP analyst schedules it in the weekly payment run and files the approval email with the invoice.
Who approves the invoice before the AP analyst schedules it?

notes.summary: Captured the reported invoice intake, PDF storage, Excel log and duplicate check, coding/allocation review, and post-approval scheduling and filing. The approval, payment-run execution, and overall finish remain unclear.

topics.answer: The process is called Accounts Payable.
The result Accounts Payable is intended to produce for the firm or client is not established.

The described work begins when an invoice is received; the account does not specify who receives it or the cadence or fixed deadlines for the overall process.
The normal receipt cadence and any fixed processing or payment deadlines are not established.

The finished condition for Accounts Payable is not established; scheduling an approved invoice in the weekly payment run is a reported step, not evidence that payment or the overall process is complete.
The role accountable for the AP result is not established; Preparer, manager reviewer, and AP analyst are named for particular actions but not identified as accountable for the overall result.

A Preparer confirms the attachment is an invoice, identifies the client/entity, records receipt for processing, and, for an urgent request, identifies its requested timing and who must approve the exception. Every received invoice is added to the processing list.
A Preparer saves the invoice PDF in the approved client/entity Box location, uses the applicable naming convention, and links or references the stored PDF in the operational log where the template supports it. The stored PDF is used as the source for approval, the Entrilia entry, and the final record comparison.
After saving the PDF, a Preparer enters vendor, invoice number, date, amount, entity, and status in the Excel invoice log and searches existing records for the same vendor + invoice number + amount. Any possible duplicate must be resolved before the invoice is recorded in Entrilia or paid.
A Preparer determines the general-ledger account, accounting class, and how the amount should be split among legal entities. The Preparer applies only a current, client-approved allocation matrix where one exists, and documents the coding reason and supporting records needed for review; a manager reviews judgment-based coding before final approval/payment.
After the invoice is approved, the AP analyst schedules it in the weekly payment run and files the approval email with the invoice. How the payment run is executed and what happens afterward are not described.

Every received invoice is added to the processing list. For an urgent request, the Preparer identifies the requested timing and who must approve the exception; the account does not state the approval outcome or what is blocked pending approval.
The Preparer searches existing Excel invoice log records for the same vendor + invoice number + amount. The invoice must not be recorded or paid until any possible duplicate is resolved; how a possible duplicate is resolved is not described.
A manager reviews judgment-based coding before final approval/payment. Where an allocation matrix is used, it must be current and client-approved. The account does not describe what the manager checks or who gives final approval.

For One Rock matrix items, the stated invoice-level support for line items above $1,000 is obtained only after the process owner or appropriate process expert confirms that the threshold and matrix version are current. The account does not establish the GPFS standard, added effort, charging, or whether this difference could be removed.
Painful, time-consuming, or error-prone work and workarounds have not been described.
Consequences of an AP error, delay, or failed control have not been described.

The invoice PDF is stored in the approved client/entity Box location and used as the source for approval, the Entrilia entry, and the final record comparison. The operational log template supports linking or referencing the stored PDF; its location and custodian are not stated.
The Excel invoice log records vendor, invoice number, date, amount, entity, and status and is searched for possible duplicates using vendor + invoice number + amount.
The approval email is filed with the invoice after approval. The account does not identify where it is filed or who performs the filing.

The work identifies a client/entity for each invoice and may split amounts among legal entities; an allocation matrix is used where one exists. The applicable entity types, process boundary, and whether the described route is general GPFS practice or client-specific are not established.

Coding and allocation use the determined general-ledger account, accounting class, and legal-entity split. A current, client-approved allocation matrix is applied where one exists; the coding reason and supporting records needed for review are documented. The source of other coding rules and how conflicting sources are resolved are not stated.
For One Rock matrix items, invoice-level support for line items above $1,000 is obtained only after the process owner or appropriate process expert confirms that the threshold and matrix version are current. The account does not identify the underlying authority or how the confirmation is recorded.
An approval is a prerequisite to the AP analyst scheduling an invoice in the weekly payment run; who approves it and the approval handoff mechanism are not established.

The described work uses Box for the invoice PDF, an Excel invoice log, and Entrilia for an invoice entry. The account does not identify a system of record or the source from which the invoice arrives.
Invoice counts, peak volumes, exception frequency, and effort are not established; a weekly payment run is reported, but no invoice volume is given.
